RUSTSEC-2026-0441 is an informational notice that the pin-utils crate is unmaintained and identifies no patched release. Milvus includes pin-utils 0.1.0 transitively through futures-util and hyper (and, in Milvus 3.0, the AWS Smithy runtime crates in the milvus-storage bridge); removing it requires those upstream crates to drop the dependency and remains under evaluation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0441.html

RUSTSEC-2026-0410 is in the malloc/free shim zstd-sys supplies to the bundled zstd C library on WebAssembly. zstd-sys compiles that shim only for wasm32 (the module is gated on cfg(target_arch = "wasm32") and build.rs enables it only for wasm32-unknown-unknown and wasm32-wasi); Milvus is built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, where the shim is not compiled and the C library uses the system allocator. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0410.html and https://docs.rs/crate/zstd-sys/2.0.9+zstd.1.5.5/source/src/lib.rs

RUSTSEC-2026-0406 is a use-after-free when changing a multithreaded context with an unfinished frame in zstd-safe, fixed in zstd-safe 7.4.0. Milvus includes zstd-safe 6.0.6 and 7.0.0 through the zstd 0.12 and 0.13 crates used by its Tantivy text-index binding. The binding pins zstd-sys to exactly 2.0.9 (zstd 1.5.5, the zstd release the Milvus C++ core links), zstd-safe 7.4.0 requires zstd-sys 2.0.17 or later, and the zstd 0.12 line used by one Tantivy fork cannot take zstd-safe 7 at all, so the fix is an upstream dependency change under evaluation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0406.html

CVE-2026-111959 (GHSA-gqmm-qrjq-4c7h) is an out-of-bounds read in Apache Arrow Rust, fixed in arrow 57.3.2 and 58.4.1. Milvus 3.0 includes arrow-data 56.2.0 through the arrow 56 crates that the milvus-storage bridge and its parquet 56 dependency require; both fixed releases are semver-incompatible with arrow 56, so the fix is an upstream arrow migration of the bridge under evaluation. The arrow 57 and 58 copies in the same bridge are at their fixed releases. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gqmm-qrjq-4c7h

CVE-2026-18140 (GHSA-8ffr-xgwf-xj56) is uncontrolled recursion in aws-smithy-json's unknown-key skip path, fixed in aws-smithy-json 0.62.7; the advisory describes a remote denial of service against smithy-rs generated servers. Milvus 3.0 includes aws-smithy-json 0.61.9 through aws-config and the AWS SSO, SSO OIDC and STS clients in the milvus-storage bridge, which use it to parse credential responses from AWS endpoints. Those client releases accept only the 0.61 line, and moving them is an AWS SDK upgrade across the bridge that remains under evaluation. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8ffr-xgwf-xj56

Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. That change resets the stream input pointer and available input after a failed write() in gz_write(), so a later gz* write cannot use the stale caller buffer. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844

RUSTSEC-2024-0449 reports that unsafe-libyaml is archived and unmaintained after its c2rust translation of libyaml, with no patched releases beyond 0.2.11. Milvus ships it transitively through serde_yaml in the embedded Tantivy binding Cargo graph compiled into the milvus Debian packages this image installs. Replacing it requires upstream dependency migrations to a maintained safe-Rust YAML stack and a package rebuild; that work remains under evaluation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0449.html

RUSTSEC-2021-0153 is an informational notice that the encoding crate is unmaintained and identifies no patched release. Milvus 2.6.23 includes it transitively through lindera-dictionary, whose only located encoding API references are in a documentation-only asset path rather than Milvus production execution. Removing the dependency cleanly still requires an upstream Lindera dependency migration and remains under evaluation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2021-0153.html

RUSTSEC-2024-0384 is an informational notice that the instant crate is unmaintained and identifies no patched release. Milvus 2.6.23 includes it through measure_time in the legacy Tantivy fork used for V5 index compatibility; migrating that fork to std::time remains under evaluation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0384.html

RUSTSEC-2025-0141 is an informational notice that the bincode crate is unmaintained and identifies no patched release. Milvus 2.6.23 includes bincode 1.3.3 transitively through Lindera for dictionary serialization; replacing it requires an upstream format and API migration and remains under evaluation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0141.html

RUSTSEC-2025-0057 is an informational notice that the fxhash crate is unmaintained and identifies no patched release. Milvus 2.6.23 includes it transitively through jieba-rs in its embedded Tantivy binding; migrating to rustc-hash requires an upstream jieba-rs dependency migration and remains under evaluation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0057.html

RUSTSEC-2026-0253 affects lru's LruCache::pop method. Both Tantivy forks embedded in Milvus use LruCache only through new, get, put, and len; neither invokes pop, and their cache keys are usize values without the advisory's panicking Drop prerequisite. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0253.html, https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/bc211a5a76930b120b1eeb25073be27f20ba0387/src/store/reader.rs#L35-L81, and https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/96f3335ab5f061926c5b44cf246e81243e1dedc5/src/store/reader.rs#L72-L118 The milvus-storage bridge in Milvus 3.0 wraps lru 0.16.4 in its GlobalLruCache, which calls get and put only with String keys, so the same conclusion holds there. See https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus-storage/blob/3ae6ac424b8dd3b7dcd06698f6779bb87e269dee/cpp/src/format/bridge/rust/src/cloud_provider_cache.rs

RUSTSEC-2026-0002 (GHSA-rhfx-m35p-ff5j) affects lru's IterMut implementation. Both Tantivy forks embedded in Milvus use LruCache through new, get, put, and len only; neither calls iter_mut, so the vulnerable iterator is not in the executable path. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rhfx-m35p-ff5j, https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/bc211a5a76930b120b1eeb25073be27f20ba0387/src/store/reader.rs#L35-L81, and https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/96f3335ab5f061926c5b44cf246e81243e1dedc5/src/store/reader.rs#L72-L118

RUSTSEC-2026-0186 affects memmap2 range-advice and range-flush methods. Both Tantivy forks embedded in Milvus use Mmap::map and full-mapping Mmap::advise, and neither calls any affected range method, so the vulnerable code is not in the executable path. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0186.html, https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/bc211a5a76930b120b1eeb25073be27f20ba0387/src/directory/mmap_directory.rs#L37-L58, https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/bc211a5a76930b120b1eeb25073be27f20ba0387/src/directory/mmap_directory.rs#L121-L127, https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/96f3335ab5f061926c5b44cf246e81243e1dedc5/src/directory/mmap_directory.rs#L37-L58, and https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/96f3335ab5f061926c5b44cf246e81243e1dedc5/src/directory/mmap_directory.rs#L121-L127

CVE-2023-49092 (RUSTSEC-2023-0071, the Marvin attack) is a timing side channel in the rsa crate's private key operations with no patched release as of rsa 0.9.10. Milvus 3.0 includes rsa through reqsign in the milvus-storage bridge, which uses it only to sign Google Cloud Storage and Oracle OCI requests with the operator's own service account key; the exposure is limited to those deployments and remains under evaluation while upstream tracks a constant-time implementation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071.html

RUSTSEC-2026-0195 is unbounded namespace declaration allocation in quick-xml's NsReader, fixed in quick-xml 0.41.0. Milvus 3.0 includes the 0.37, 0.38 and 0.39 lines through reqsign (AWS credential responses), opendal (Azure Blob, Azure Data Lake and GCS services) and lance in the milvus-storage bridge, which parse XML returned by the configured object storage; each of those crates pins its quick-xml line below 0.41, so the fix is an upstream dependency migration under evaluation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0195.html

RUSTSEC-2026-0194 is quadratic run time in quick-xml's duplicate attribute check on a start tag, fixed in quick-xml 0.41.0. Milvus 3.0 includes the 0.37, 0.38 and 0.39 lines through reqsign (AWS credential responses), opendal (Azure Blob, Azure Data Lake and GCS services) and lance in the milvus-storage bridge, which parse XML returned by the configured object storage; each of those crates pins its quick-xml line below 0.41, so the fix is an upstream dependency migration under evaluation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0194.html

CVE-2026-43868 (GHSA-2f9f-gq7v-9h6m) is an excessive allocation on a size value read by the Rust thrift protocol decoder, fixed in thrift 0.23.0. Milvus 3.0 includes thrift 0.17.0 through the parquet crates (56, 57 and 58) that the milvus-storage bridge uses to read Parquet footers, and every parquet release the bridge's dependencies (lance, iceberg, paimon) accept pins thrift 0.17, so moving it is an upstream dependency migration under evaluation. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2f9f-gq7v-9h6m

CVE-2026-25537 (GHSA-h395-gr6q-cpjc) is a type confusion in jsonwebtoken's claim validation, reached through decode and Validation::validate. Milvus 3.0 includes jsonwebtoken through reqsign in the milvus-storage bridge, whose Google service account token flow only calls jsonwebtoken::encode to mint the assertion it sends to Google; no code path decodes or validates a token, so the vulnerable validation logic is not in the executable path. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h395-gr6q-cpjc and https://docs.rs/crate/reqsign/0.16.5/source/src/google/token/service_account.rs

CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

Waiting for upstream Linux-PAM to ship a constant-time fix for the pam_userdb plaintext-password timing leak (Debian security tracker marks [trixie] as postponed, minor issue; no fix available in any Debian release). The vulnerable path requires pam_userdb to be configured with crypt=none or no crypt= argument, which DHI images do not configure. This pam package is present only in dev images that include apt tooling; runtime images are not affected by this package-level finding.
